title: Heterogeneous Adversarial Audit SOP — Internal Operational Distillation

claims.text: Union-merge of audit findings has lower blocker miss-rate than majority-vote merge, because voting can eliminate real blockers that only one auditor caught.
Refute-first prompting (assume the work is wrong, try to prove it) captures more true blockers per run than neutral review prompting.
Requiring path:line or command-output evidence per finding reduces LLM hallucinated blockers compared to free-text evidence.
Convergence is reached reliably when HIGH+CRITICAL count is monotonically non-increasing across rounds and two consecutive rounds produce zero new blockers.

hypotheses.text: Union-merge produces fewer missed HIGH/CRITICAL blockers per run than majority-vote merge on the same artifact set.
Refute-first prompt suffix increases blocker capture rate without increasing false-positive rate relative to neutral audit prompt.
Mandating path:line evidence in the prompt reduces unsupported_claim_rate in findings JSON.

anti_patterns.name: same-family self-audit
anti_patterns.description: Using the same model family for both producer and auditor invalidates the audit. Heterogeneous runtime pairing is mandatory.

anti_patterns.name: vote-to-merge-findings
anti_patterns.description: Merging audit findings by majority vote silently drops real blockers. Findings must be union-merged; host decides per-item.

anti_patterns.name: historical-contrast hallucination
anti_patterns.description: LLM auditors shown before/after diffs re-hallucinate the old state as the current state and report false blockers. Prompts must describe the CURRENT state only; historical context must be stripped before auditor sees artifact.

anti_patterns.name: rubber-stamp PASS
anti_patterns.description: An auditor that returns no findings is not evidence of quality; it is evidence of a weak audit posture. Empty findings should trigger a re-run with stronger refute-first prompt.
